pr_title: planner, unistore: support index scan for common handle on unique index
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #18284 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

There are 6 index value layouts in total:
  - (> 9 bytes) new collation non-unique
  - (> 9 bytes) new collation unique int handle
  - (> 9 bytes) new collation unique common handle
  - (<= 9 bytes) old collation non-unique
  - (<= 9 bytes) old collation unique int handle
  - (> 9 bytes) old collation unique common handle

In unistore, the value length is not enough to distinguish whether an index value is a new collation or not. Thus, __Old collation unique common handle__ is processed incorrectly.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/ffc1bcaaa7fc49e8ef173cd8d2dd0c2a1a5ebc4a/store/mockstore/unistore/cophandler/closure_exec.go#L625-L630

This PR adds common handle support for `indexScanProcessNewCollation`.

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: [xxx](url) <!-- REMOVE this line if not applicable -->

- reuse the logic of `DecodeIndexKV` in `tablecodec`.
- add a simple test case.

issue_context.title: clustered index: 'invalid codec version' when select with unique key
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
set @@tidb_enable_clustered_index=true;
drop table if exists t;
create table t (a varchar(64), b varchar(64), uk int, v int, primary key(a, b), unique key uuk(uk));
insert t values ('a', 'a1', 1, 11), ('b', 'b1', 2, 22), ('c', 'c1', 3, 33);
select * from t use index (uuk);
```
<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```
+---+----+----+----+
| a | b  | uk | v  |
+---+----+----+----+
| a | a1 | 1  | 11 |
| b | b1 | 2  | 22 |
| c | c1 | 3  | 33 |
+---+----+----+----+
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```console
(1105, 'invalid codec version')
```
